pattern_id: Crash-recovered safety lock regression enables conflicting HotStuff 3-chains
description: In Aptos SafetyRules, SafetyData (including last_voted_round, preferred_round, and one_chain_round) is persisted separately from BlockStore / QC state. Under a crash window where a validator V has signed a higher-round vote on branch A (e.g., A2 at round r2) but the updated SafetyData is not durably persisted, V can restart from stale SafetyData that only reflects an older lock (e.g., after voting for A1 at r1). After restart, when a Byzantine leader equivocates and drives a conflicting branch B with a QC chain at higher rounds, SafetyRules may construct and sign a new vote for a conflicting block B3 at round r3, because it only enforces local monotonicity of last_voted_round and preferred_round based on the stale SafetyData. The implementation does not cross-check against previously signed votes across crash boundaries, nor does it recompute locks from the high-QC chain in storage. As shown in consensus/safety-rules/src/tests/crash_recovered_lock_regression_conflicting_3chain.rs, this allows an adversary with a single Byzantine validator (in n=4, f=1) to obtain two conflicting QCs (for A2 and B2) and, in a full HotStuff deployment, extend them into two conflicting 3-chains that can both commit at the same height, violating safety.
trigger_condition: 1) BFT consensus with SafetyRules persisting SafetyData separately from block/QC storage; 2) An honest validator V signs a vote at round r2 on branch A, but crashes in a window where SafetyData has not yet durably recorded the new lock; 3) After restart, SafetyRules is reinitialized from stale SafetyData (e.g., last_voted_round = r1 < r2, preferred_round, one_chain_round not reflecting the new lock) while BlockStore or external state may reflect higher QCs; 4) A Byzantine leader equivocates and drives a conflicting branch B with higher-round QCs; 5) SafetyRules is asked to construct_and_sign_vote_two_chain for a block B3 at round r3 on the conflicting branch.
test_template: 1) Construct a small validator set (e.g., n=4, f=1) or a single-validator abstraction and create a genesis QC and EpochState; 2) Initialize a SafetyRules instance with a starting SafetyData (epoch, last_voted_round = r0, preferred_round = 0, one_chain_round = 0, last_vote = None); 3) Build a branch A: A1 at r1 and A2 at r2, with appropriate QCs so that a valid 2- or 3-chain lock is formed; 4) Have SafetyRules.construct_and_sign_vote_two_chain vote for A1 and then A2, capturing the true post-A2 SafetyData; 5) Simulate a crash by discarding this SafetyRules instance and re-creating a new SafetyRules from a manually crafted, stale SafetyData that only records a vote up to A1 (last_voted_round = r1, last_vote = vote(A1), preferred_round/one_chain_round <= r1); 6) Build a conflicting branch B: B1 at r1, B2 at r2, B3 at r3, with QCs that form a valid chain conflicting with A; 7) Ask the restarted SafetyRules to construct_and_sign_vote_two_chain for B3; 8) The protocol is correct if this returns an error or a vote whose proposed block ID equals the previously voted A2; the protocol is vulnerable if it returns an Ok(Vote) for B3 with a different block ID, demonstrating that V can now sign for two conflicting branches and that an adversary can combine votes from honest + Byzantine validators to form two conflicting QCs / 3-chains.
